title: Maps & Cartography
description: The art of the map — gilded old-world atlases, decorative city views, and celestial charts.

items.title: Typus Orbis Terrarum
items.description_narrative: This influential world map, 'Typus Orbis Terrarum,' was a foundational piece in Abraham Ortelius's groundbreaking atlas. It presents the known continents and oceans of the 16th century, reflecting the era's expanding geographical understanding.
items.tags: world map, cartography, renaissance, 16th century, geography, exploration, atlas

items.title: Nova et Aucta Orbis Terrae Descriptio
items.description_narrative: This map, titled 'Nova et Aucta Orbis Terrae Descriptio', is a seminal work by Gerardus Mercator. It is renowned for its innovative use of the Mercator projection, which revolutionized navigation by representing compass bearings as straight lines.
items.tags: cartography, world map, Mercator projection, navigation, exploration, historical map

items.title: Universalis Cosmographia
items.description_narrative: This monumental 1507 world map, the Universalis Cosmographia, represents a significant advancement in cartography during the Age of Exploration. It is historically notable as the first known map to use the name "America" for the New World.
items.tags: world map, cartography, exploration, Renaissance, geography, historical, Americas

items.title: Nova Totius Terrarum Orbis Geographica
items.description_narrative: This intricate world map, 'Nova Totius Terrarum Orbis Geographica', was created by the renowned Dutch cartographer Willem Blaeu. It offers a detailed geographical representation of the known world, characteristic of 17th-century Dutch cartography.
items.tags: world map, cartography, dutch golden age, willem blaeu, historical map, geography, decorative
items.credit_line: This map is available from Eran Laor Cartographic Collection of the National Library of Israel. link to the source:NOVA TOTIUS TERRARUM ORBIS GEOGRAPHICA AC HYDROGRAPHICA TABULA

items.title: Americae Nova Tabula
items.description_narrative: This intricately detailed map, "Americae Nova Tabula," presents a comprehensive depiction of the American continents as understood in the early 17th century. Created by the renowned Dutch cartographer Willem Blaeu, it reflects the evolving geographical knowledge and exploration of the New World during its time.
items.tags: map, cartography, Americas, exploration, 17th century, Dutch, atlas, geography

items.title: Fra Mauro map
items.description_narrative: The Fra Mauro map is a monumental 15th-century mappamundi that encapsulates the known world from Europe to Asia and Africa. Crafted by the Venetian monk Fra Mauro, it is notable for its detailed geographical information, reflecting the knowledge of its time, and its distinctive south-up orientation.
items.tags: world map, cartography, medieval, venetian, geography, 15th century, parchment, historical
items.credit_line: https://www.highres.factum-arte.org/Fra_Mauro_Map/shared/viewer.html (downloaded with dezoomify-rs and cropped with vips)

items.title: Tabula Rogeriana
items.description_narrative: The Tabula Rogeriana is a highly detailed world map and geographical text created by the Arab geographer Muhammad al-Idrisi. Commissioned by King Roger II of Sicily, it synthesizes classical Greek and contemporary Arab geographical knowledge, depicting the known world of the 12th century with remarkable accuracy for its time.
items.tags: world map, cartography, medieval, geography, Islamic scholarship, Sicily, history

items.title: Leo Belgicus
items.description_narrative: The Leo Belgicus is a distinctive map of the Low Countries, ingeniously rendered in the form of a heraldic lion. This allegorical cartography by Claes Janszoon Visscher combines geographical information with a powerful symbol of national identity.
items.tags: cartography, historical map, Netherlands, allegory, lion, symbolic, national identity

items.title: Ptolemy world map
items.description_narrative: Claudius Ptolemy's world map, from his influential work *Geographia*, represents a landmark early attempt to systematically map the known world based on mathematical principles. Though often depicted in later reproductions, this ancient map reflects the geographical understanding of the Greco-Roman world and significantly impacted European cartography for over a millennium.
items.tags: ancient, cartography, geography, classical, scientific, world map, historical

items.title: Harmonia Macrocosmica: Planisphaerium Copernicanum
items.description_narrative: This work by Andreas Cellarius, titled Harmonia Macrocosmica: Planisphaerium Copernicanum, illustrates the Copernican model of the universe. It is a significant plate from his renowned celestial atlas.
items.tags: cosmology, astronomy, Copernican system, celestial, scientific illustration, early modern

items.title: Harmonia Macrocosmica: Planisphaerium Ptolemaicum
items.description_narrative: This intricate celestial map, "Planisphaerium Ptolemaicum," visually depicts the geocentric model of the universe as understood by Claudius Ptolemy. Part of Cellarius's grand star atlas, its elaborate design and vibrant hand-coloring exemplify Baroque-era scientific illustration and cartography.
items.tags: celestial map, astronomy, ptolemaic model, geocentric, 17th century, baroque, cartography, dutch golden age

items.title: Harmonia Macrocosmica: Northern Constellations
items.description_narrative: This intricate plate from the Harmonia Macrocosmica atlas meticulously illustrates the northern constellations with artistic detail and astronomical precision. It serves as a prime example of 17th-century celestial cartography, combining scientific understanding with imaginative artistry.
items.tags: astronomy, constellations, cartography, celestial map, scientific illustration, star chart, historical

items.title: Uranometria: Orion
items.description_narrative: Uranometria: Orion is a celestial map from Johann Bayer's groundbreaking star atlas, first published in 1603. This detailed copperplate engraving depicts the constellation Orion, a prominent figure in the night sky, with stars marked according to Bayer's innovative nomenclature.
items.tags: astronomy, celestial map, star atlas, constellation, engraving, scientific illustration, early modern
items.credit_line: From WP en, uploaded by en:User:Mouser

items.title: Firmamentum Sobiescianum
items.description_narrative: This monumental celestial atlas, "Firmamentum Sobiescianum," was created by the pioneering astronomer Johannes Hevelius. It meticulously charts the constellations with remarkable detail, presenting a comprehensive view of the night sky.
items.tags: astronomy, celestial, constellations, cartography, scientific illustration, star atlas

items.title: Atlas Coelestis
items.description_narrative: This monumental celestial atlas meticulously charts the positions of thousands of stars, representing a significant advancement in astronomical cartography. It compiles the precise observations of John Flamsteed, England's first Astronomer Royal, and was published posthumously.
items.tags: astronomy, celestial, atlas, cartography, stars, scientific illustration, 18th century

items.title: Civitates Orbis Terrarum: Constantinople
items.description_narrative: This intricate engraving presents a detailed bird's-eye view of Constantinople, illustrating its significant urban features and strategic location. It is part of a monumental six-volume city atlas, one of the earliest and most comprehensive of its kind.
items.tags: cityscape, map, engraving, constantinople, historical, cartography, urban view, 16th century
items.credit_line: This map is available from Eran Laor Cartographic Collection of the National Library of Israel. link to the source:Byzantium, nunc Constantinopolis

items.title: Carta Marina
items.description_narrative: Olaus Magnus's Carta Marina is one of the earliest and most accurate maps of Northern Europe, depicting the Nordic countries with significant detail. Beyond its cartographic innovations, the map is renowned for its vivid illustrations of sea monsters, land animals, and ethnographic observations.
items.tags: map, cartography, renaissance, northern europe, scandinavia, sea monsters, woodcut, historical

items.title: A New and Accurate Map of the World
items.description_narrative: This intricately detailed world map by John Speed offers a comprehensive view of global geography as understood in the early 17th century. Beyond its geographical information, the map is adorned with elaborate decorative elements, including allegorical figures, celestial diagrams, and inset vignettes, characteristic of the period's grand cartographic works.
items.tags: cartography, world map, 17th century, exploration, decorative, historical, geography

items.title: Nova Belgica et Anglia Nova
items.description_narrative: This intricately detailed map, 'Nova Belgica et Anglia Nova,' visually charts the early colonial territories of New Netherland and New England in North America. Willem Blaeu's renowned work offers a crucial cartographic perspective on European exploration and territorial claims during the 17th century.
items.tags: map, cartography, colonial history, new netherlands, new england, dutch golden age, 17th century
items.credit_line: From: Blaeu, W., Atlas Maior, (Amsterdam: Blaeu) 1643. Geographicus - https://www.geographicus.com/P/AntiqueMap/NovaBelgicaetAngliaNova-blaeu-1634-2

items.title: Asiae Nova Descriptio
items.description_narrative: Asiae Nova Descriptio is a foundational map presenting the Asian continent, reflecting the geographical understanding of its era. This significant work was created by Abraham Ortelius for his seminal Theatrum Orbis Terrarum, widely regarded as the first modern atlas.
items.tags: map, cartography, Asia, Renaissance, early modern, geography, historical, atlas
